reported.name: half-cut exponent
reported.says: the links crossing the cheapest cut into halves found, as a power of the number of agents: 2/3 for a body of three dimensions, near 0 for a bottleneck, near 1 for a folded small world

reported.name: half-cut exponent of the random twin
reported.says: the same for the world's random twin, which is no space at all

reported.name: same-position share
reported.says: of two agents put in the same situation, how often they stake measurably differently

reported.name: effective kinds of staking
reported.says: how many kinds of staking the agents fall into, counted by their shares

reported.name: doctrine alike
reported.says: the share of agents making the more common choice between spreading their stake and staking it all on one place

reported.name: having a child
reported.says: the share of agents that have a child in an iteration

reported.name: agents
reported.says: how many agents the world holds

criteria.name: alive
criteria.asks: played to the end of its run (3,000 iterations in round 3) and never down to 20 agents

criteria.name: decentralised
criteria.asks: no agent linked to more than 5% of the others, and 3 to 12 links per agent

criteria.name: resilient
criteria.asks: at least 80% of the agents in the 2-core, and no single agent's loss cuts off more than 15% of the world, nor a single link's more than 15% (the rules keep a world in one piece)

criteria.name: almost three-dimensional
criteria.asks: a typical distance at least 1.3 times its random twin's, and a dimension of 2 to 5

criteria.name: diverse
criteria.asks: statistic by statistic: fewer than 80% of the agents hold the same number of tokens, and some agent holds more than 3; fewer than 80% of the 2-core's agents have the same number of links; fewer than 80% have the same age, and fewer than 80% the same genotype; and fewer than 95% make the same choice, to have a child or not

criteria.name: not too even
criteria.asks: a Gini of the tokens of at least 0.46 (B2's most even world in Experiment 16)
